      "VIETNAM\nGEOGRAPHY\nArea\nTotal: 331,210 sq km Land: 310,070 sq km Water: 21,140 sq km\nClimate\ntropical in south; monsoonal in north with hot, rainy season (May to September) and warm, dry season (October to March)\nNatural Resources\nantimony, phosphates, coal, manganese, rare earth elements, bauxite, chromate, offshore oil and gas deposits, timber, hydropower, arable land\nGOVERNMENT\nChief of State\nPresident Nguyen Phu TRONG\nHead of Government\nPrime Minister Nguyen Xuan PHUC\nGovernment Type\ncommunist state\nCapital\nHanoi\nLegislature\nunicameral National Assembly or Quoc Hoi (500 seats; 5-year terms)\nJudiciary\nSupreme People's Court (consists of the chief justice and 13 judges)\nAmbassador to US\nAmbassador Ha Kim NGOC\nUS Ambassador\nPEOPLE & SOCIETY\nPopulation\n98.7 million (July 2020 est.)\nPopulation Growth\n0.84% (2020 est.)\nEthnicity\nKinh (Viet) 85.7%, Tay 1.9%, Thai 1.8%, Muong 1.5%, Khmer 1.5%, Mong 1.2%, Nung 1.1%, Hoa 1%, other 4.3% (2009 est.)\nLanguage\nVietnamese (official), some English, French, Chinese, Khmer, mountain area languages\nReligion\nBuddhist 7.9%, Catholic 6.6%, Hoa Hao 1.7%, Cao Dai 0.9%, Protestant 0.9%, Muslim 0.1%, none 81.8% (2009 est.)\nUrbanization\nurban population: 37.3% of total population (2020) rate of urbanization: 2.98% annual rate of change (2015-20 est.)\nLiteracy\n95% (2018)\nECONOMY\nEconomic Overview\nsince transitioning in 1986 from a centrally planned, agrarian economy to a more industrial and market based economy, Vietnam has raised incomes substantially and seen strong growth, primarily due to increases in domestic demand and strong manufacturing exports\nGDP (Purchasing Power Parity)\n$648.7 billion (2017 est.)\nGDP per capita (Purchasing Power Parity)\n$6,900 (2017 est.)\nExports\n$214.1 billion (2017 est.) partners: US 20.1%, China 14.5%, Japan 8%, South Korea 6.8% (2017 est.)\nImports\n$202.6 billion (2017 est.) partners: China 25.8%, South Korea 20.5%, Japan 7.8%, Thailand 4.9% (2017 est.)\nas of August 2020"

      "Close\nThis content was created and maintained as part of a past project. As of April 6 2026, it is no longer being updated.\nVietnam Flag for Vietnam\nCountry Spotlight\nVietnam is not known to have ever developed biological, chemical, or nuclear weapons. Since the Vietnam War, it has been vocal in supporting the complete elimination of chemical weapons and signed the Chemical Weapons Convention in 1993. Vietnam possesses a limited ballistic missile arsenal but does not indigenously produce them.\nSee Vietnam's performance in\n* Nuclear Security Index\n* Global Health Security Index\n  Region East Asia and the Pacific\n  2013 High enriched uranium reserves transferred to Russia\n  11 million Gallons of Agent Orange herbicide used by U.S. forces during Vietnam War\n  2014 Signed a 123 bilateral nuclear cooperation agreement with the U.S. which expires in 2044\nNuclear\n* Is a member of Treaty of Bangkok , which established a nuclear weapon-free zone in Southeast Asia\n* Adopted a nuclear energy law in 2008 as a legal framework for nuclear activities\n* Constructing two nuclear power plants in Ninh Thuận province to be completed by 2030, after initially shelving the project in 2016\n* Signed agreements in 2025 with Russia and Japan on nuclear energy cooperation, and Russia plans to construct a nuclear power plant in Vietnam\nBiological\n* Has never possessed a biological weapons capability\n* Party to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety\nMissile\n* Possesses Scud ballistic missiles acquired from the USSR and North Korea and has sought upgrades from international partners\n* Developing anti-ship cruise missiles and possesses surface-to-air missile systems\n* Plans to purchase BrahMos anti-ship cruise missiles from India for $700 million\nChemical\n* Has never possessed an offensive chemical weapons capability and supports their universal elimination\n* Was subjected to herbicide attacks from the U.S. between 1962 and 1971, though these are not considered chemical weapons by the OPCW\nTreaties and Regimes Memberships"
